answer: Like mycelium weaving forest soil into living bedrock, decentralized trust resists artificial clones through an interconnected web of mutual staking. A sybil horde resembles a shifting dune, easily blown away by recursive web-of-trust consensus: validating an identity requires organic endorsement paths, casting the fable of effortless mass duplication aside. Like stalks of yarrow cast in an ancient divination, each query requires peer co-signatures, imposing an exponential cost on any attacker attempting to manufacture artificial consensus.
